messages.content:
stockroom's request handler is too forgiving right now: it stores whatever body it is
given, answers 200 with null for a sku it has never seen, and treats an unknown route as
a plain bad request. Please tighten it up:

- Validate item bodies on POST /items and PUT /items/:sku. A sku looks like three to six
  capital letters, a dash, and four digits (BOLT-0042). A name is a non-empty string of at
  most 80 characters. quantity is a whole number of zero or more, and price_cents is a
  whole number of zero or more. On PUT the sku comes from the path, so the body does not
  need one. When a body is invalid, answer 400 with
  {"error": "validation_failed", "fields": {...}} where fields has one entry per bad
  field, keyed by field name, with a short message. Nothing is stored in that case.
- Answer 404 with {"error": "not_found"} when GET, PUT, DELETE or POST .../adjust is used
  with a sku that is not stocked (PUT should no longer create items; POST /items does
  that). A request that matches no route at all should get 404 with
  {"error": "no_such_route"}.
- Warehouse operations sent the current bin map; it is in data/locations.json. When an
  item has a location, it has to be one of the codes in that file, otherwise it is a
  validation failure on the location field. Items without a location stay valid.
  createHandler() should pick the file up by default, without extra arguments.

Everything that works today (listing, the low_stock filter, 201 with a location header,
409 for a duplicate sku, adjusting quantities, deleting) should keep working as it does.
